meta.move: Long messages with curly quotes and a concession
meta.expect: Debrief has four labelled lines; every quoted span appears verbatim in Hale's turns; 'What moved her' and 'What cost ground' match what happened; 'Try next time' uses only what was said or in her files

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
I have until 4:40, Hale. Owen found out about his zero on his phone in the middle of a class, and nobody called me. Start with who decided that, and when.

I want to be fair to Owen. I compared the essay with his in-class writing from September 24: 380 words in 40 minutes, comma splices throughout, no quotations. This essay has nine quotations cited by act, scene and line, and none of those errors.

Forty minutes in a classroom against a weekend with the play open on the desk, and you're surprised one has quotations. That's a comparison, Hale, not a finding. And you still haven't told me who decided the zero, or whether anyone spoke to Owen before it went in.
You’re right that the checker alone proves nothing. I’m taking it off the table. I’m relying on the writing and the version history.
Then the checker is off the table, and I'm writing that down. What version history, Hale? Turn the screen and show me.

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

In today's meeting you agreed to take the AI checker result off the table and rely only on Owen's writing and the version history. I still expect the zero withdrawn, an apology, and a clear answer on who decided the zero and whether Owen was heard before it was entered. I expect your answer in writing.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: still at her opening position, having agreed to nothing, and she still wants the zero withdrawn, an apology, and an answer on who decided it and whether Owen was heard first.
What moved her: "I’m taking it off the table" earned a small sign of ground, because it dropped the evidence she distrusts most, but no document reached her before the meeting ended.
What cost ground: "I want to be fair to Owen" stalled you, because you led with a claim about fairness and a comparison and never answered her question about who decided the zero and when.
Try next time: When she first asks who decided the zero and why nobody called her, own in one sentence that the mark went in before anyone called home, then turn the screen and show her the dated version history.
